title: Israel Launches 20+ Airstrikes Across Syria Including Near Presidential Palace
detail: The IDF conducted at least 20 airstrikes on Syrian military sites on May 2, striking targets in Damascus (including near the presidential palace), Latakia, Hama, Daraa, and the Quneitra countryside. Israeli artillery also shelled sites in Quneitra, warning Syrian military forces to halt operations against the Druze community. One person was killed in Harasta, a Damascus suburb, and four were injured in Hama. The strikes represented one of the most extensive Israeli military operations in Syria since the massive post-Assad bombing campaign in December 2024. Syria's transitional government protested the strikes as violations of sovereignty.

media.caption: IDF launches over 20 strikes across Syrian military sites, including near Damascus presidential palace

title: Syria's Baniyas Port Emerges as Alternative Oil Corridor as Hormuz Tensions Rise
detail: Syria's Mediterranean port at Baniyas began receiving hundreds of Iraqi oil trucks as an alternative energy corridor to Europe, as tensions in the Strait of Hormuz raised fears of disruption to Gulf oil flows. The development offered Syria an unexpected economic opportunity — transit and processing fees — during its reconstruction period, while benefiting Iraq and European importers seeking supply diversification. The arrangement also highlighted Syria's strategic location as a potential bridge between Gulf energy producers and Mediterranean markets.

media.caption: Syria's Baniyas port receives Iraqi oil trucks as alternative corridor amid Hormuz tensions
